title: Reflex Testing Protocols by Service Class — Laboratory Test Orders
content:
A reflex test on Laboratory Test Orders is a second test the laboratory performs automatically when the result of the first test meets the laboratory's reflex criterion. Each service class states whether it performs and charges reflex tests at all, and which first test leads to which reflex test.

| Service class | Reflex tests performed and charged | First test → reflex test |
|---|---|---|
| Routine Clinical Testing | Yes | 899 TSH with Reflex to Free T4 → 866 Free T4 (reflex); 5463 Urinalysis, Complete, with Reflex to Culture → 395 Urine Culture (reflex) |
| Specialty Clinical Testing | Yes | 249 ANA Screen, IFA, with Reflex to Titer and Pattern → 4377 ANA Titer and Pattern (reflex) |
| Esoteric Reference Testing | No | none |
| Molecular Infectious Disease Testing | No | none |
| Clinical Toxicology Testing | Yes | 90895 Prescription Drug Monitoring Screen → 94177 Definitive Drug Testing, 1-7 Drug Classes |
| Anatomic Pathology & Cytology | Yes | 91384 ThinPrep Pap Test with Reflex to HPV (ASC-US) → 14424 HPV mRNA E6/E7, High Risk; 14424 HPV mRNA E6/E7, High Risk → 14460 HPV Genotypes 16, 18/45 (reflex) |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | No | none |

## Notes on the table

- A class marked "No" has no reflex pairs at all; its tests are performed as ordered only.
- In Anatomic Pathology & Cytology the HPV mRNA E6/E7 test (14424) appears on both sides of the table: it is the reflex test of the Pap test and is itself followed by the genotyping reflex (14460).
- Every reflex pair stays inside one service class: the reflex test is a test of the same class's menu.

**Example (hypothetical).** A Specialty Clinical Testing accession carrying the ANA Screen (249) whose result meets the reflex criterion is followed by the ANA Titer and Pattern (4377); a Molecular Infectious Disease Testing accession never has a reflex test, because that class performs none.
